Paragraph: In Bhagavad Gita Chapter 18, Verse 66, Krishna offers his ultimate reassurance to Arjuna: 'Abandon all varieties of dharmas and simply surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions and distress; do not fear or grieve.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Overwhelming moral anxiety, fear of consequences, and cognitive overload from complex choices.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna offers divine grace and ultimate surrender (Saranagati), inviting Arjuna to release his burdens and trust in the Divine.
Outcome/Resolution: Surrendering worries brings deep emotional relief, peace, and freedom from existential fear.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Saranagati / Prapatti (Complete self-surrender to divine grace)
Abhaya-Pradana (Divine promise of absolute protection and fearlessness)
Moksha (Liberation from psychological and spiritual bondage)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The ultimate message of the Gita: surrender all burdens to the Divine, who grants complete protection and liberation from fear.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Reflects the psychological benefit of relinquishing excessive control, finding peace through trust and surrendering existential burdens.
